## Description

<!-- SECTION:DESCRIPTION:BEGIN -->
MEASURED 2026-08-23 on schimmer-glanz.exe.xyz while establishing what SMS still needs.

/etc/nfc/env begins:

  # NFC TimeSheets backend environment
  # GENERATED by ops/sync-secrets.sh from the psst vault (tag: server). Do not hand-edit:
  # the next sync overwrites this file. Change the value in the vault and re-run instead.

ops/sync-secrets.sh IS NOT IN THIS REPOSITORY and is not in /srv/nfc/ops/ on the box either
(checked both). Whatever wrote that header was never committed.

WHY IT MATTERS RIGHT NOW, not abstractly. The file today carries APP_KEY, DATABASE_URL,
GOOGLE_GEOCODING_KEY and PORT. The psst vault (tag: server) carries TWILIO_SID and
TWILIO_SECRET, which are NOT on the box. So the vault and the box already disagree, and the
one document that explains how to reconcile them names a program that does not exist. The
next person who needs to add a credential -- Twilio's Account SID and sender are exactly that
case (decision-48, TASK-243) -- reads 'do not hand-edit', looks for the script, does not find
it, and either hand-edits anyway against the file's own instruction or stalls.

There is also a silent-drift hazard: SENTRY_DSN went unset in production for months
(TASK-44/TASK-224) and this is the mechanism by which that stays invisible -- nothing compares
the vault to the box.

WHAT TO BUILD
- ops/sync-secrets.sh: render /etc/nfc/env from 'psst list --tag server' over ssh, atomically
  (write a temp file, chown root:app, chmod 0640, mv), then systemctl restart nfc-api.
  No secret may be echoed, and it must refuse rather than write a partial file.
- A --check mode that DIFFS the vault against the box by KEY NAME ONLY (never values) and
  exits non-zero on drift, so ops/deploy.sh or a timer can gate on it.
- The negative case is the whole point and must be seeded: remove a key from the box, watch
  --check go RED, restore, watch it go GREEN.

DO NOT let this quietly become 'a script that overwrites production's environment' without
a backup: it must copy the existing file aside first, exactly as ops/prove-sms-live.sh does
around its seeded credential test, and verify the restore by sha256.

ALTERNATIVE, IF THIS IS NOT WANTED: delete the lie instead. Rewrite the header to say the
file is hand-maintained and where the canonical copy is. A comment that misdirects is worse
than no comment. Either outcome closes this task; leaving the header as it is does not.
<!-- SECTION:DESCRIPTION:END -->
